record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.original_question: For non-unique factorisations [[P,Q(P)]]=♦(P,[[P,P]]) of the Poisson-cocycle condition through Leibniz graphs, what is the topological structure of the resulting identities ♦₂−♦₁≡0? Equivalently, if one forms a meta-graph whose vertices are Leibniz graphs and where adjacency means that two Leibniz graphs have expansions sharing a Kontsevich oriented graph, what are the genus, diameter, typical cycle length, and related invariants of these meta-graphs, and how does the iterative generation algorithm saturate them?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Let us say that two Leibniz graphs are adjacent if their expansions have a Kontsevich orgraph in common. Now, describe the topological structure of the identities ♦2 − ♦1 ≡ 0 for known non-unique solutions of the factorisation problems. Otherwise speaking, describe the meta-graphs with Leibniz graphs as vertices: what is their genus, diameter, typical cycle length, etc. ? • Investigate the saturation curve for the number of Leibniz graphs produced by the iterative algorithm (e.g., see [9, Table 1]): at which stage are the new Leibniz graphs typically leaves vs handles ? What are the last new Leibniz graphs in this sense ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $P$ be a Poisson bivector on a finite-dimensional affine manifold, with Schouten bracket $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$, so that $[\![P,P]\!]$ is the Jacobiator (a tri-vector that vanishes on Poisson structures). Following the Kontsevich graph calculus, an oriented Kontsevich graph on $n$ "aerial" vertices encodes a poly-differential operator built from copies of $P$; a Leibniz graph is an oriented graph in which exactly one internal vertex carries the tri-vector $[\![P,P]\!]$ (with three outgoing edges, satisfying the Leibniz rule), while all other internal vertices carry $P$. Each Leibniz graph $L$ has a canonical expansion $\mathrm{Exp}(L)$ as a finite linear combination of Kontsevich oriented graphs obtained by resolving the Jacobiator vertex via the Leibniz rule.
   
For a Kontsevich-graph cocycle $\gamma$ producing a flow $\dot P = \overrightarrow{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)$, the Poisson-cocycle condition $[\![P,\overrightarrow{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)]\!]=\diamondsuit(P,[\![P,P]\!])$ admits in general non-unique factorisations through Leibniz graphs: one may have two distinct Leibniz-graph linear combinations $\diamondsuit_1,\diamondsuit_2$ both balancing the equation, yielding identities $\diamondsuit_2-\diamondsuit_1\equiv 0$ in the space of Leibniz graphs.
   
Define the Leibniz meta-graph $\mathcal{M}$ as follows: vertices of $\mathcal{M}$ are Leibniz graphs (in a given combinatorial type/order), and two Leibniz graphs $L,L'$ are joined by an edge for each Kontsevich oriented graph appearing in both $\mathrm{Exp}(L)$ and $\mathrm{Exp}(L')$ (multi-edges allowed).

Problem. For each known non-unique factorisation of the Poisson-cocycle condition through Leibniz graphs (e.g. those arising from the tetrahedral, pentagon-wheel, and heptagon-wheel cocycles), determine the topological/combinatorial structure of the resulting identities $\diamondsuit_2-\diamondsuit_1\equiv 0$. Concretely, describe the corresponding Leibniz meta-graph $\mathcal{M}$: compute or estimate its genus, diameter, typical cycle length, and other natural graph invariants. Furthermore, analyse the saturation behaviour of the iterative algorithm that generates Leibniz graphs balancing such factorisations: at which stage do newly-produced Leibniz graphs typically appear as leaves of $\mathcal{M}$ versus as handles (i.e. closing new cycles), and characterise the last Leibniz graphs to be produced before saturation.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as one of the open problems posed in the Kontsevich graph framework for Poisson-bracket symmetries. Subsequent work by Buring, Kiselev, Rutten and collaborators (2019–2025) has extended computations of cocycles (tetrahedral, pentagon-wheel, heptagon-wheel) and Leibniz-graph factorisations and discussed Leibniz meta-graphs, but no published work appears to give a systematic determination of the genus, diameter, typical cycle length, or saturation behaviour of these meta-graphs. The status is therefore consistent with the problem still being open.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, V. Implementation
status_evidence.snippet: Two Leibniz graphs are adjacent vertices in the Leibniz meta-graph if the expansions of these Leibniz graphs have at least one Kontsevich oriented graph in common, and multiple edges are allowed in the meta-graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The Leibniz meta-graph construction is still an active object of investigation in 2025, without a complete description of its topology.

status_evidence.title: Poisson Brackets Symmetry from the Pentagon-Wheel Cocycle in the Graph Complex
status_evidence.snippet: Factorisations [[P,Or(gamma)(P)]] = diamondsuit(P,[[P,P]]) through Leibniz graphs are non-unique.
status_evidence.claim: Non-unique factorisations producing identities among Leibniz graphs are documented but their meta-graph topology is not analysed.

status_evidence.title: The heptagon-wheel cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of cocycles and associated Leibniz-graph identities.
status_evidence.claim: Further cocycle examples giving rise to non-unique Leibniz-graph factorisations have been computed, but the topological invariants of the corresponding meta-graphs are not addressed.
